A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoAI framework and retain matching method equations and core experiments. Text, tables, figures and appendices support a reliable comparison. v1's explicitly unfinished depth-results table is a manuscript limitation, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative novel-view synthesis experiments, component ablations and geometry evaluations in Tables 1–4, alongside qualitative results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative robustness tests, large-model comparisons and reference-view-count results, plus new qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The dual diffusion branches, aggregated attention, image-to-geometry attention instillation, mesh conditioning and camera-space normalization are retained. Equations (1)–(8) change notation rather than procedure. The newly described image-only operation and alternative-predictor evaluation do not establish a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual qualitative evaluation on NAVI and on previously untrained Cityscapes and MegaDepth data (Appendix B.1 and B.3). This substantially broadens evaluation to urban and in-the-wild scenes. The original training datasets and DTU, RealEstate10K and Co3D evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Figure 7 expands the LVSM comparison to include VGGT, ZeroNVS and both 16-frame and 25-frame ViewCrafter configurations. New Table 7 evaluates ViewCrafter and LVSM quantitatively on DTU. v1's dedicated LucidDreamer/GenWarp appendix comparison figure is removed, although both methods remain in Table 1.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs introduce Gaussian point perturbations at 3–15%, random masking at 30/50/80%, alternative geometry predictions from DepthAnything V3, runtime/memory measurements and a 1–7-reference-view Co3D sweep. The stated extrapolation definition also changes to camera positions only. Original training settings and described DTU/RealEstate10K view-sampling procedures remain; the PDFs do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds controlled geometry-noise and sparsity tests, greater-than-90-degree occlusion/shading examples, and cross-predictor alignment validation (Section 4.4; Appendix B.2, B.4–B.5). It adds a 1–7-view Co3D analysis alongside retained Table 4. Existing component and normalization ablations remain, while the provisional depth-accuracy comparison is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experimental results. v3's Gaussian standard deviations specify input perturbations, not statistical uncertainty in measured performance.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical entries. New Table 7 reports DTU PSNR of 14.04 for ViewCrafter versus 15.56 for MoAI with one view, and 15.23 for LVSM versus 15.58 for MoAI with two views. Tables 5–6 add perturbation results, and Table 8 reports Co3D PSNR increasing from 14.62 to 23.45 across 1–7 views. New qualitative and runtime findings are also reported. v1's provisional depth-comparison Table 5 is removed; these changes do not demonstrate improved same-setting performance between versions.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces v1's convex-combination definition over SE(3) camera poses with a convex hull of camera positions, explicitly ignoring viewing direction. This substantively corrects and narrows the mathematical definition of extrapolation. The method equations otherwise remain equivalent, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: aligned pose-free image/geometry synthesis through attention instillation and mesh conditioning, strong extrapolation, competitive interpolation and generalization. Rewording and additional supporting evaluations do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 refines the explanation of complementary image/geometry attention, qualifies that positional extrapolation may expose unseen regions, and adds interpretations concerning predictor-independent alignment and the geometry-versus-speed trade-off (Appendix A.2 and B.5). It removes the provisional depth-accuracy discussion. These extend the retained mechanism account rather than replace it.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.2 reports A6000 hardware, 9.81-second/28GB joint two-view generation and 4.3-second/14GB image-only operation. Most training and implementation details match v1. The abstract replaces the project-page link with a statement that code and weights will be publicly released, changing the documented access information without establishing an actual release.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to ZeroNVS, ViewCrafter, DepthAnything 3, NAVI, Cityscapes and MegaDepth, with limited expansion of its positioning against large generative models. The broader relationship to feedforward, generative and warping-and-inpainting approaches remains unchanged. The switch to author-year citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, mechanism explanations and results prose undergo broad rewriting and condensation. Related-work subsections become run-in headings, references move before the appendices, and appendix material is reorganized. A new Appendix C discloses LLM writing assistance. These constitute substantial editorial and structural revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 7 is rebuilt as a larger comparison with timing annotations; new figures and tables display robustness, domain, alignment and baseline evaluations. The reference-view illustration moves to Appendix Figure 18 and expands to 1–7 views. Existing normalization, component-ablation and scene-completion material is retained or rearranged, while v1 Figure 12 and its provisional depth table disappear. Typography, captions and table layouts also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the empirical assessment of the unchanged method: modern baseline comparisons, controlled geometry-corruption tests and broader domain/predictor evaluations address important gaps in v1's evidence for competitiveness and robustness. Computational reporting and the corrected extrapolation definition also improve assessability. Trade-offs remain: the provisional depth comparison is removed without an equivalent quantitative replacement, and claims of minimal degradation overstate Tables 5–6, including a PSNR decline from 15.580 to 13.000 at 80% masking. Nevertheless, the added comparative and diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net quality improvement.
